metaDescription: Five cordless hedge trimmers under $150 from Ryobi, Greenworks, Craftsman and Black+Decker, compared on brushless motors, platforms and cut capacity.
expertTake: The Greenworks 24V 20-inch brushless is the best overall for its 4000 SPM cut and 1.1-inch capacity. The Black+Decker 22-inch 20V is the value pick for its bundled battery. Anyone who already owns a Ryobi or Greenworks 40V battery should buy the matching tool-only trimmer and skip the kits.
introParagraphs: The jump to this budget is mostly a jump in platforms. The trimmers here run on the same battery families as mowers, blowers and drills, so buying one is as much a decision about which battery system you want to live with as about the trimmer itself. A trimmer's battery is its fuel tank, so pick the platform you will keep.

The cap here is $150, and prices move, so it reflects listing prices when this guide was updated. Compared with cheaper tiers, you gain brushless motors, faster blades and a stronger bite on thicker branches. Choose with the battery in mind first and the blade second.

products.name: Greenworks 24V 20-Inch Brushless Hedge Trimmer with Debris Collector
products.description:
The Greenworks trimmer is the only brushless tool in this lineup, driving a 20-inch dual-action steel blade at 4,000 strokes per minute with a stated cutting capacity of 1.1 inches. A brushless motor wastes less energy as heat and has no carbon brushes to wear, so the trimmer gets more work from each charge and the motor should outlast a brushed one. The 2.0Ah battery and charger are included.

The 4,000 SPM figure is much higher than the 2,400 to 2,800 SPM claimed for budget cordless trimmers, and the faster stroke gives a cleaner shear on soft growth. A built-in debris collector sweeps clippings aside, and a wrap-around handle allows multi-position cutting.

It gives up two inches of blade against the 22-inch Black+Decker, but its capacity is nearly 50 percent greater than that machine's three-quarter-inch rating. Keep the blade clean, oil it lightly and store the 24V battery indoors. It suits owners who want the best cut quality and a motor with the longest likely life. In year three the battery is the part most likely to fade, so buy a spare while the platform is still stocked and keep the debris collector clear. Compared with the Craftsman, the Greenworks wins on cutting quality but is not a platform pick unless you plan to add 24V tools.
products.bestFor: Owners who want the cleanest cut and a long-lived brushless motor.
pros: Brushless motor wastes less energy and wears less
4000 SPM blade gives a clean shear
1.1 inch stated capacity is the highest here
cons: 20 inch blade covers less per pass than 22 inches

products.name: Black+Decker 20V Max 22-Inch Cordless Hedge Trimmer
products.description:
The Black+Decker is the value pick: a 22-inch dual-action blade, a three-quarter-inch capacity and a battery and charger in the box. It claims up to 40 percent less vibration than single-action blades and enough runtime for roughly 3,000 square feet of hedge per charge.

It uses a brushed motor, which is simpler and cheaper but less efficient than the Greenworks brushless design. Against that machine it offers two more inches of blade for less capacity, so it trims a long, level hedge faster but struggles on stiff stems.

The 20V platform covers many other Black+Decker tools, so spare packs are easy to buy. Wipe and oil the blades after use and avoid forcing it into branches near its capacity limit. Charge the pack after each session and keep a second battery on the charger for big jobs. Compared with the Greenworks 24V, it is the better choice when your hedge is long and soft and you want to finish in fewer passes.
products.bestFor: Long, level hedges of soft growth on a budget.

products.name: RYOBI 18V ONE+ 22-Inch Dual-Action Hedge Trimmer
products.description:
The RYOBI 18V ONE+ trimmer joins one of the largest battery platforms in home tools, with a 22-inch dual-action blade. The listing gives little detail, so confirm whether a battery and charger are included before buying, because many ONE+ trimmers ship as bare tools.

The main reason to choose it is the platform. If you already own ONE+ batteries, the trimmer costs a fraction of a full kit, and the same packs power blowers, mowers and drills. If you do not, the platform lock-in is a cost.

Against the Black+Decker, the blade length is equal, and the real difference is battery ecosystem. Keep the blades clean and the pack indoors. If you already own ONE+ packs, the economics are straightforward, and the tool will outlast several batteries. If your RYOBI batteries are already in the shed, treat the trimmer as an add-on and check capacity on the box.
products.bestFor: Owners already invested in the RYOBI ONE+ battery family.
pros: Joins a very large battery platform
Spare packs and chargers are common
cons: May be sold without battery or charger

products.name: Greenworks 40V 24-Inch Cordless Hedge Trimmer, Tool Only
products.description:
The Greenworks 40V trimmer combines a 24-inch dual-action blade with a one-inch cutting capacity, the longest blade and second-highest capacity in this lineup. A three-sided wrap-around auxiliary handle with a cushioned overmold grip allows cutting in many positions.

It is sold tool-only, so the price excludes the battery and charger. For owners of Greenworks 40V mowers or blowers the trimmer is the cheapest way to add capacity; for everyone else, a 40V pack has to be added to the cost.

Compared with the 24V brushless Greenworks, it trades the faster stroke for a longer blade and more voltage headroom. It is heavier at the tip, so use short sessions. Oil the blades and keep the battery indoors. Because it is heavier at the tip, use both hands and take breaks to protect your shoulders. It is the right tool for formal hedges that rarely get overgrown, and the wrong one for renovation cutting.
products.bestFor: Greenworks 40V owners who want a long, capable trimmer.
pros: 24 inch blade covers a lot per pass
40V platform shares packs with other tools
cons: Battery and charger are not included

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 20-Inch Cordless Hedge Trimmer Kit
products.description:
The CRAFTSMAN V20 trimmer comes as a kit with battery and charger, a 20-inch dual-action steel blade and the V20 platform shared with a range of garden and workshop tools. A 20-inch blade is a mid-size choice: lighter at the tip than a 24-inch, more productive than 17 or 18 inches.

It does not state a high capacity or an advanced motor, so it competes on platform and balance. Against the Black+Decker it has two inches less blade and a similar brushed-motor character.

It is a fair choice if you already use V20 tools. Oil the blades and store the battery inside. Over time the V20 packs are easy to replace, which keeps the tool serviceable long after the original battery fades. For an owner who values a familiar platform over the last bit of cutting speed, it is a calm, sensible purchase.
products.bestFor: V20 platform owners who want a balanced mid-size trimmer.
pros: 20 inch blade balances reach and weight
cons: Capacity and motor not highlighted on the listing
Less blade than the 22 or 24 inch models

buyingCriteria.explanation: A brushless motor, as on the Greenworks 24V, has no brushes to wear and wastes less energy as heat, so it extends runtime and motor life. For a trimmer used a few weekends a year, the difference is small; for weekly use it adds up. Brushless tools also run quieter, which neighbors appreciate. Heat is what kills small motors, and brushless designs shed less of it than brushed ones. In practice, a brushless trimmer also holds its speed when the blades meet a thicker stem, where a brushed motor slows and the cut turns ragged.

The Greenworks lists 4000 SPM, far above the 2,400 to 2,800 SPM claimed on budget trimmers. A faster stroke shears softer growth cleanly. It does not raise the thickness limit, which is set by the blade gap. Trim in steady sweeps so the high stroke rate does the work. If you cannot feel the blade bite cleanly on a test stem, the stroke speed is not the problem; a dull edge is. Stroke speed is also why the hedge looks flatter and more even after a single pass.

The Greenworks 24V reaches 1.1 inches and the 40V 1 inch, while the Black+Decker stays at three quarters. Thicker capacity means fewer trips for loppers. Never rely on capacity as an invitation to force wood. Cut thicker stems with loppers first for a cleaner result. Cut capacity is also a measure of how tightly the blade teeth are spaced.

A trimmer is a battery decision. RYOBI ONE+ and Greenworks 40V packs power many other tools. Tool-only listings like the Greenworks 40V cost far more if you start without a pack. Check that the voltage on the tool matches the battery you own. Packs for older platforms stay available longer than packs for brand-new ones. Check how many tools you could run from the same battery before settling on a platform.

A 24-inch blade covers about 20 percent more than 20 inches but adds tip weight. Choose by how long you trim at one stretch. Try to hold the trimmer level for a full minute in a store before buying. A heavier trimmer with a rotating handle often feels lighter than a lighter one without. If you trim for more than twenty minutes at a time, consider rotating handles and a lighter blade.

The Greenworks 24V, Black+Decker and Craftsman ship with a battery and charger. The Greenworks 40V is tool-only, and the RYOBI listing is unclear. Check before comparing. Always confirm the kit contents with the seller. Ask yourself whether you want to pay for a battery you may already own.

cards.label: Brushless
cards.text: The Greenworks 24V runs cooler, lasts longer and cuts at 4000 SPM.

cards.label: Brushed
cards.text: The Black+Decker and CRAFTSMAN are simpler and cheaper, with lower stroke speed and capacity.

howToChoose.note: Pick brushless for frequent use, brushed for occasional trims.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Capacity near one inch, a fast stroke and a strong gearbox.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Greenworks 24V at 1.1 inches and the Greenworks 40V at 1 inch are the best choices.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You trim often, own a large hedge, or want a brushless motor like the Greenworks 24V.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You trim a small hedge twice a year, where the Black+Decker kit suffices.

maintenance.why: Resin builds up and stalls the motor. Spray with blade oil to protect against rust. Wipe away resin with a rag and a little solvent. Do this even if you only trim twice a year.
Loose bolts cause uneven cutting. Use a tight-fitting driver for blade bolts. A drop of threadlocker keeps blade bolts in place. Check them after the first hour of use.
Temperature extremes degrade lithium cells. Charge the battery to about half before long storage. Do not leave batteries in a hot car.
Packed clippings add weight and block movement. Pull clippings out with a stick, not your hand. Wear gloves when clearing it.
Grease seepage signals a worn seal. Keep the trimmer upright so oil does not run into the motor. If grease seeps, stop using it until it is serviced.

faq.a: For frequent use, yes. It runs cooler, uses charge better and lasts longer. For occasional trims, a brushed motor is fine. A brushless motor also tends to run cooler under load. Owners who trim weekly report the difference most. Over several seasons the savings in battery wear are real.

Yes, if you do not own the battery. Add the battery and charger before comparing. Confirm what is in the box before comparing prices. Check the seller listing, not only the title. A tool-only listing is only a bargain if you have the right battery already.
Up to the stated capacity, such as 3/4 to 1.1 inches. Thicker needs loppers. Cut thick stems at an angle for a cleaner, healthier wound. Thicker stems also need a sharper blade than soft ones.
